aspects.says: On a Deque, push, pop, peek and poll use the head and add and offer the tail, so add with pop is a queue; pop on an empty deque throws while poll returns null, and ArrayDeque refuses null.
basis: section:Which End a Deque Method Uses

aspects.says: A PriorityQueue's iterator, toString and stream follow its heap array, so only peek and poll see the order, and ties come out in no particular order.
basis: section:A PriorityQueue Is Ordered Only at Its Head

aspects.says: LinkedList.add(index, x) and get(i) walk node by node to the index, so ArrayList is faster even at inserting in the middle; LinkedList wins only when inserting at a position an iterator already holds.
basis: section:LinkedList Loses to ArrayList Unless You Already Hold the Position

aspects.says: TreeMap's range methods return live views that refuse keys outside their range, and a TreeMap or TreeSet treats keys whose compareTo is 0 as the same key, whatever equals says.
basis: section:TreeMap Answers "Which Key Is Nearest?", Compares with compareTo, and Returns Live Views

aspects.says: TreeMap's floor and ceiling include an equal key and lower and higher don't, floorEntry returns null below the first key, and the two-argument subMap excludes its upper bound.
basis: section:TreeMap Answers "Which Key Is Nearest?", Compares with compareTo, and Returns Live Views

aspects.says: java.util.Stack extends Vector: it iterates bottom-first, exposes the List API, and pays for synchronized calls even with one thread, while ArrayDeque with push iterates from the top.
basis: section:ArrayDeque Is the Stack and the Queue; Stack Is a Synchronized Vector

aspects.says: HashMap turns a crowded bin into a tree ordered by hash and then by compareTo, so colliding keys stay cheap to look up only when their class is Comparable of itself with an order that separates unequal keys.
basis: section:Colliding HashMap Keys Stay Fast Only When They Are Comparable

aspects.says: A bin already holding 8 entries becomes a tree on the next insert only once the table has 64 buckets; a smaller table is doubled instead.
basis: section:Colliding HashMap Keys Stay Fast Only When They Are Comparable
aspects.reason: HashMap's internal layout is visible only by reflection into java.util, which a graded practice can't rely on

aspects.says: Timings without JMH need a warm-up, a consumed result and several runs, and only their ratios are worth reading.
basis: section:A Timing Loop That Warms Up First
aspects.reason: a method of measuring, not behaviour a deterministic test can check; timings vary between machines and runs
